set.name: Asmalı Meyhane
set.hook: A 1950 meyhane on the bazaar street, grilling island squid and serving raw fish with basil.
set.why: Niko Manalodis and his brothers opened it in 1950, and the house still cooks the island way: kalamar laid on the coals rather than battered, and raw fish dressed with basil, the two plates Daily Sabah says you find only here. Yemek.com describes the room through its details: painted stairs, a resident cat and an old record player, with a meze counter of walnut octopus, fennel cuttlefish and stuffed courgette flowers.
set.verdict: Order the grilled kalamar and the raw fish and let the counter choose the rest; that is where the kitchen is strongest. Online reviews are mixed, with praise for the meze and the staff and complaints about price and slow service at busy times. Go early in the evening, before the summer crowd fills the stairs.
set.signature: Grilled island kalamar, then raw fish with basil.
set.caveat: No 2026-dated evidence and no winter dates found; reviews mention high prices and uneven service on busy nights.

set.hook: A meze house inside Apostol Kalfa's old coffeehouse, on the street that was once the island bazaar.
set.why: The street was the centre of the Bozcaada bazaar, and the building was the coffeehouse of Apostol Kalfa, an islander. When it became a restaurant the owners kept what was left: tall guillotine window frames no one on the island makes any more, a hand-planed ceiling and cedar floorboards. Tables spill under vines and flowers outside. The meze list runs to island herb salad, the house borani and mastic-scented artichokes.
set.verdict: Yemek.com calls it an island classic, and every guide we found sends you here for the meze and the squid rather than for a view. It is a lane, not a harbour terrace. Evenings are hard to get even in September and October, so book days ahead in season and call to confirm it is open out of season.
set.signature: Sandal borani and the island herb salad, then grilled squid.
set.caveat: Book days ahead for dinner in season; no 2026-dated evidence or winter dates found.

set.hook: A seafood and meze house in Cumhuriyet, with dinner under a yediveren rose tree.
set.why: The table that wins the reviews eats under a yediveren, the repeat-flowering rose, trained over the courtyard. The cold meze arrive first, then the house meze the island calls the Bozcaada Bombası, served nowhere else, and then grilled fish. Diners talk about the owners working the room and about how clean the place is, which counts for a lot on an island of summer pop-ups.
set.verdict: On review volume and score it is the most-praised table on the island right now (Restaurant Guru 4.9 from about 4,660 votes; Foursquare is cooler at 7.7). Treat it as the long dinner, not a quick stop: meze first, then fish. Book a day or two ahead in summer. We found nothing dated 2026 and no winter dates, so call before you go.
set.signature: The Bozcaada Bombası, then grilled sea bass.
set.caveat: Book ahead for summer and holiday dinners; no winter or 2026 dates found, call first.

set.hook: A family home-cooking kitchen started by retired teachers, known for its mantı.
set.why: Retired primary-school teachers opened it more than forty years ago, and it still cooks like a house kitchen: dolma and vine-leaf sarma that diners compare with a grandmother's, stuffed courgette flowers in season, and the mantı people come back for, pinched small and served with yoghurt. The owners take their time with visitors who speak no Turkish, pointing at the pots.
set.verdict: Come for lunch and the mantı; it is the reason to cross town, and the olive-oil vegetables are the reason to stay. Do not expect a sea view or a fish grill. The evidence is reviews without dates, so treat the details as likely rather than certain, and check it is open before planning around it.
set.caveat: Home cooking with no sea view; no 2026-dated evidence or winter dates found, call ahead.

set.hook: Red-and-white checked cloths on Alsancak Sokak, and octopus with artichokes in cream.
set.why: You spot it by the red-and-white checked tablecloths on the lane. Oggusto puts it at about ten years old; Yemek.com already calls it an island classic. The plate people write about is enginarlı ahtapot, octopus and fresh artichoke in a cream sauce with a note of rosemary, the kind of thing a cook invents rather than inherits. Sea bass wrapped in vine leaves and seafood-stuffed mussels follow.
set.verdict: The cheaper, looser alternative to the set-piece meze houses, and the place for a cook's own dishes rather than the island canon. Order the octopus with artichokes. Reviews on the room are mixed, so come for the plates. Nothing found is dated 2026 and no winter dates exist online, so call before you go.

set.caveat: Small, plain room with mixed reviews on comfort; no 2026-dated evidence or winter dates found.

meyhane.title: Squid, rakı and meze lanes
meyhane.story: Bozcaada's meyhanes sit on two short streets in the town centre, not on the harbour. On Çınar Çarşı, Asmalı Meyhane has grilled island kalamar on coals and served raw fish with basil since Niko Manalodis and his brothers opened it in 1950. Around the corner on Alsancak Sokak, the old bazaar street, Sandal fills Apostol Kalfa's former coffeehouse, keeping its cedar floors, and lists island herb salad and mastic artichoke among its meze. A few doors along, Nevreste seats dinner under a yediveren rose tree and opens with the Bozcaada Bombası, a stuffed meze no other house makes. The rhythm is the same everywhere: cold meze, hot meze, then fish, with rakı.
meyhane.where: Asmalı Meyhane, Çınar Çarşı Caddesi; Sandal, Alsancak Sokak; Nevreste, Alsancak Sokak

home.title: Mantı and the cook's plates
home.story: Away from the fish grills, Bozcaada eats from pots: dumplings, olive-oil vegetables, leaves rolled round rice, the food of the Turkish and Rum households that shaped the town. Dört Hanımeli was opened more than forty years ago by retired primary-school teachers, and reviewers still come for its mantı, its vine-leaf sarma and stuffed courgette flowers. On Alsancak Sokak, Ada'm, about ten years old, shows what an island cook does with the same pantry, putting octopus with artichokes in a cream sauce and wrapping sea bass in vine leaves. Both are plain rooms where the plates are the point, cheaper than the courtyard meze houses, and best at lunch.
home.where: Dört Hanımeli, Bozcaada town; Ada'm, Alsancak Sokak
